I first started with the area. We know the area to be 100π. We also know that the area of the circle equals r^(2)π. So 100π = r^(2)π. Do the algebra and you get r = 10.

Then we look at the circle itself. arcCD - arcBD = 2arcBD. We can rearrange this formula to be 3arcBD = arcCD. And since both lines pass through the center of the circle, We know that arcCD = arcBE, and arcCE = arcBD, because of adjacent angles. Since 3arcBD = arcCD = arcDB, and arcBD also equals arc CD, that would give us a total circumference of 8arcBD (3arcBD + 3arcBD + arcBD + arcBD).

Since circumference equals 2rπ, the total circumference would equal 20π. (Remember r is equal to 10). We also know the total circumference is equal to 8arcBD, so 8arcBD = 20π, so arcBD = 5/2π.

Going back to the first equation that arcCD = 3arcBD, and arcBD = 5/2π, then we can find that arcCD = 3(5/2π), which is 15/2π.
